content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents Curvphormer, a Curvature-based topology-aware Graphormer, that incorporates Discrete Ricci Curvature (DRC) into the graph-based Transformer architecture. Curvphormer aims to learn the structural information of graphs and expand the expressiveness of graph models. Experiments on three datasets with different scales and tasks are conducted to validate the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

(+)The structure of this paper is clear.

(+)The figures in this paper are helpful in making readers better understand the concepts.

(+)Experiments are conducted on three datasets with different scales. Code will be released upon publication.

Weaknesses:

(-) The novelty of the proposed method is limited. The contributions of this paper mainly focus on replacing the SPD(Shortest Path Distance) structural encoding method applied in the Graphormer [1] with a DRC encoding method. 

(-) Technical details need to be explained better. Some notations in the equations and experiment results need to be clarified. 

(-) More ablation studies/sensitivity analysis would be helpful to better support the proposed method. For example, it may be worth studying the performance of the model if weights are assigned to the edge attribute information and the DRC-based structural information instead of simple addition, or the effect of removing one or more inputs  (like node degrees, edge features…), etc.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Quality:

The paper has a clear structure. Figures are illustrative and well-drawn. However there are some grammatical errors/misusages of words, for example, in the abstract part, it should be “expands the expressiveness” instead of “expands the expressive”; in the third paragraph of introduction, “ graph represent learning” should be graph representation learning”, and so on. 

The quality of the paper can be further improved by including more ablation studies or sensitivity analysis (e.g. study the effect of changing the weights of different features, removing the DRC features…).

Also, the reviewer suggests the authors check the format of the bibliography. There are some omissions/formatting errors (e.g. the first reference has no author information).

Clarity: 
More clarifications or explanations need to be made in the methods and experiment sections, including: 
1) In equation 1), what does the tilde sign in “x~y” mean? If that means x approximates y, it is not clarified in the paper how the approximation between two nodes is defined. 
2) In Table 2, what do “validMAE” and “testMAE” mean? If we assume they mean MAE evaluated on the validation set and the test set, is there any particular reason to report the result on the validation set instead of the test set? More clarifications are needed here. 

Originality:
It’s interesting that the author uses DRC as a new source of structural information to enhance the expressiveness of graph-based transformer models. However, the proposed method is more of an incremental work that is built heavily upon the original work of Graphormer [1]. Thus the novelty of the method presented in this paper is limited. 

[1] Chengxuan Ying, Tianle Cai, Shengjie Luo, Shuxin Zheng, Guolin Ke, Di He, Yanming Shen, and Tie-Yan Liu. Do transformers really perform badly for graph representation?
content.summary_of_the_review: The reviewer decided to make a reject recommendation to this paper mainly due to its limited novelty and contribution. The proposed method is more of an incremental work that is built heavily upon a published work. Also, the quality of the paper can be further improved as the reviewer explained above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose to enhance graph neural network models by incorporating more complex structural information using Discrete Ricci Curvature (DRC). In particular, the authors modify the recently proposed Graphormer by using as input a suitably constructed matrix that uses structural information derived using DRC.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- Improved empirical performance over recently proposed GNN architectures
- Toy examples show intuition behind approach. It is a reasonable idea that incorporating more structural information would aid in graph-related ML tasks

Weaknesses:
- Limited novelty. DRC for GNNs has been considered before. The main contribution in this paper is using it to a recently-proposed architecture that uses transformer.
- Limited experimental evaluation. The proposed method is only evaluated in 3 datasets.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Originality: I believe there is limited novelty in the paper. It is expected that sophisticated ways of incorporating structural information would improve performance in graph learning tasks. Moreover, DRC has been proposed before in this context.

Quality: The quality of the paper is overall high. The proposed approach is interesting and reasonable.

Clarity: As someone with little background in DRC, I found the paper a little difficult to follow at times. As way of example, it wasn't clear to me if there is a typo in Equation (1) and it should be "\gamma(w_{xz})" instead of be "w_{xz}" in the denominator in the second case. Otherwise, it is not clear that the "probability distribution" adds up to 1.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This submission proposes a new graph-based Transformer architecture, namely Curvphormer, based on Discrete Ricc Curvature (DRC). The Curvphormer has more expressive power tested on different graph-based learning tasks. The main reason for the effectiveness of the proposed model is that DRC can quantify the connections in graphs to extract desired structural information. Experiments on different graph-level tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of Curvphormer.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. A new graph-based Transformer model based on DRC is proposed.
2. The experiments demonstrate that DRC is a useful feature to be used in graph-based Transformers.

Weaknesses:
1. The Ricci curvature as a useful feature for graph-based learning tasks has been explored previously. The whole novelty of this submission could be limited as it seems that DRC is just applied to graph-based Transformers.
2. The experiment results on three datasets are not enough to support the true effectiveness of the proposed model. More experimental results are needed.
3. The intuition or insightful findings of DRC + graph-based Transformers are limited. From the reviewer's perspective, Curvphormer is presented in Section 2.3.4, but there is a lack of depth discussion on this. In other words, there is no explanation for DRC is unique and effective when incorporated with a graph-based Transformer.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper presented a new graph-based Transformer method-based DRC. However, the overall novelty of this submission is limited. There also exist some presentation issues.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This submission proposes a new graph-based Transformer architecture, namely Curvphormer, based on Discrete Ricc Curvature (DRC). The Curvphormer has more expressive power tested on different graph-based learning tasks. The main reason for the effectiveness of the proposed model is that DRC can quantify the connections in graphs to extract desired structural information. Experiments on different graph-level tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of Curvphormer. However, the reviewer finds that the overall novelty of this submission is limited, and there are some presentation issues. Issues are listed as follows:

1. Section 3.1 indicates that DRC is a valuable feature to other models (GCN), not just graph-based Transformers. The reviewer wondered whether this DRC as an extra feature could be used in any other graph model. If this is the case, it would be better to design experiments to demonstrate this. 

2. Section 2.2 introduces Discrete Ricci Curvature. Unrelated definitions could just be put into the appendix. The claimed Theorem 1 seems to be a known one, which should present in the preliminary section.

3. In [1], authors proposed using Ricci Curvature for graph neural network models. The submission argued that the expressive power is limited due to over-smoothing and over-squashing problems. However, how the proposed method can overcome this issue? The effectiveness of the method is due to graph-based Transformers or others?


[1] Ye, Ze, Kin Sum Liu, Tengfei Ma, Jie Gao, and Chao Chen. "Curvature graph network." In International Conference on Learning Representations. 2019.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.

content.title: Response to reviewers
content.comment:
Dear Reviewers,

Thank you for your useful feedback on our work, and we greatly appreciate your words of affirmation. We are working on revising our manuscript based on your comments.

We admit that it is still a long way to improve our design. However, the most inspiring information we want to convey is that mathematical concepts characterize in-depth structural information effectively, proper utilization of them to a powerful NN backbone makes great difference. 
DRC is the most widely studied graph descriptor, and has been effectively used in GNN backbones. However, GNN suffers inevitable issues such as over-smoothing and over-squashing. We have done experiments to alleviate these issues with the help of DRC, but the rich information of DRC is wasted because of the drawbacks of GNN. Thus in our work, we design Curvphormer and do experiments to argue that DRC improves graph-based transformers with a great leap.
